title: The Career Mistake Smart People Make at 22 (That Costs Them at 30)
script: The career mistake most smart people make at 22 costs them everything by 30. It's not working too hard or picking the wrong boss. It's optimizing for title and culture over skills and compensation trajectory. At 22, you take the job at the cool startup because the vibes are good. At 30, you realize you have great experience and no financial runway. Two questions that would have changed everything: What skills will this make me more employable for in five years? And what does this role pay in two years versus right now? Early compounding is everything. The job title fades. The skill stack and savings rate compound.
